concept: A proof web seen at fiber scale: fine silk-like strands meet in a calm, luminous weave. Craft and connection convey rigor without machinery or a literal diagram.
composition: Use a portrait field, with the intricate crossing slightly right of center and dark negative space on the left for headline placement. Let arcs continue beyond the frame. A narrow mobile crop should retain one clear convergence and several sweeping threads. Keep shallow focus: crisp crossings at the focal area, softer filaments receding into charcoal.
strands: Use hair-fine ivory and antique-gold filaments with varied tension: some taut and bright, others matte, braided, or faint in shadow. Measured radial lines and quiet curved cross-links feel mathematically deliberate, with tiny irregularities like hand-laid silk. A few strands meet in an intricate knot while others continue outward, suggesting one proof may support many conditions. Imply no fixed count of spokes, rings, or steps.
brandConnection: Charcoal, warm ivory, and aged gold echo Moriarty’s cinematic banner. Fiber-scale precision gives Webs and Strands a tactile identity: proofs become fine, durable connections within a larger assurance. Keep the image literary and composed, suited to serif-led editorial typography.
avoid: No spider, person, city, moon, circuitry, crypto nodes, labels, formulas, or UI. Avoid neon, glitter, stock-vector symmetry, a blinding flare, and any implied three-proof or seven-step recipe.
imagePrompt: Editorial macro artwork for Moriarty Webs and Strands: a mathematically deliberate, subtly handmade web of fine silk filaments, tactile ivory and antique gold on charcoal (#14130f). Portrait-first, mobile-croppable; intricate convergence right of center, dark left-side negative space, arcs continuing beyond frame. Varied tension, matte and braided threads, selective shallow focus, warm highlights, quiet cinematic chiaroscuro. Abstract proof-bearing connections, not a diagram. No text, interface, spider, people, neon, crypto nodes, or fixed spoke count.
